detail: The same brand wordmark was exposed as the primary page asset on several manual pages; it is not an application interface and teaches no task structure.
Light-theme counterpart of the accepted Trends insight; theme substitution alone is not a materially different structure.
Light-theme counterpart of the accepted retention matrix; it would duplicate the same task and composition.
Repeated generic documentation demo image appeared on multiple product pages and did not add a page-specific structural lesson.
The official changelog page was accessed, but the linked media now returns NoSuchBucket and could not be visually validated from the primary asset.
A second wide view of the same meeting summary and action-item composition as VR-041; visual inspection found insufficient task or structural difference despite a non-matching dHash.
Isolated touch-value diagram lacks enough surrounding interface state or domain relationship for a standalone reference.
Small wiring diagram is useful inside documentation but not sufficiently complete as an independent visual reference.
Animated hand performance is promotional motion content and does not expose an operational interface structure.
The 128-pixel product thumbnail is illegible; a distinct 2048-pixel CDN variant was inspected and accepted instead.
The inspected animation mostly shows a theme toggle and long black transition frames; the official static Extra Dark app-drawer comparison carries a stronger operational lesson.
Promotional Essential Memory illustration contains icons and a decorative playback strip but no legible operational product surface.
Feature-summary graphic names six OS changes but does not expose the structure or behavior of any one interface.
Isolated first-party icon set is useful as brand documentation but insufficient as a structural interface reference.
The official screenshot includes an email-like account identifier; a safer distinct utility reference was selected instead.
The dark product image did not load behind the consent layer during visual inspection, so resolution, legibility, and integrity could not be confirmed.
